PMID:42154518.setting: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, single academic tertiary centre (four hospital sites); automated EHR-based audit
PMID:42154518.standard: NICE Quality Standard QS138 statement 2 (pre-2026 definition): adults having surgery with expected blood loss >500 mL should receive perioperative tranexamic acid

cycle2.result: Overall automated TXA compliance 86.3% (manual QI audit same period 90%, 10 cases); trauma and orthopaedics 98.2% (n = 393), cardiac surgery 83.7%, gynaecology 83.2%, urology 94.2%, colorectal 43.5%, vascular 0%. Improvement from 2024 included gynaecology +26.8% and cardiac surgery +15.6%.

PMID:42154518.other_findings: Paper is mainly a validation of an automated audit: denominator coverage 96.2%, miscoding 3.9%, WHO checklist–EPR concordance 74.2%, and manually adjudicated 'true' compliance 85.3%. Primary hip and knee replacements 98.8%, revision hip and knee 100%, neck of femur fracture fixation 96.7%; open iliofemoral and aortic operations 0%.

PMID:42342903.topic: National hip fracture audit standards compliance
PMID:42342903.setting: Irish Hip Fracture Database national clinical audit, all 16 eligible acute hospitals in Ireland (NOCA, RCSI)
PMID:42342903.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standards (seven core clinical standards, 2017; based on BOA/BGS Blue Book standards) and best practice tariff criteria; data quality target of 90% case submission

cycle1.result: Geriatrician assessment 11%, bone health assessment 65%, falls assessment 62%, surgery within 48 h 70%, admission from ED to orthopaedic ward 15%; national coverage 63%.

PMID:42342903.intervention: Establishment of the national audit with governance committee, audit manager, hospital hip fracture governance committees, quarterly dashboards with SPC charts, a QI foundation programme, a best practice tariff (€1000 per compliant case, from 2018), the Golden Hip Award, and new orthogeriatric and advanced nurse practitioner posts.

cycle2.result: Geriatrician assessment 86%, bone health assessment 90%, falls assessment 87%, surgery within 48 h 77%, admission from ED to orthopaedic ward 36%; national coverage 95%; day one physiotherapy mobilisation 74% (2018) to 85%.

PMID:42342903.other_findings: Total 41,304 cases 2013–2024; best practice tariff compliance rose from 7% (2018) to 21% (2024) and time to surgery remained the hardest standard to meet. Inpatient mortality fell from 5% to 4% and new long-term care admission from 6% to 3%.

PMID:39237920.setting: Orthogeriatric unit (experimental) versus conventional orthopaedic unit (control), Grenoble Alpes University Hospital; controlled before/after audit and feedback study
PMID:39237920.standard: Unit pain protocol: routine acetaminophen 1 g three times a day (3 g/day) during the three postoperative days

cycle1.dates: December 2018 to April 2019 (before intervention, started May 2019)
cycle1.result: Postoperative 3 g/day acetaminophen 16% (16/99); preoperative 9%; nurse adherence to acetaminophen prescriptions 13% preoperatively and 13% postoperatively.

PMID:39237920.intervention: Audit and feedback with nurses: two 1-hour pain teaching sessions, distribution of a pain assessment scale, protocol updated to 'give acetaminophen regardless of pain assessment', medicine staffing reviewed with clinical pharmacy, and night/weekend standby with a Saturday ward round.

cycle2.result: Postoperative 3 g/day acetaminophen 60% (60/100) (OR 8.55, p < 0.001; versus control OR 6.76, p < 0.001); preoperative 16% (p = 0.13); nurse adherence 32% preoperatively and 52% postoperatively.

PMID:39237920.other_findings: Control unit showed no change (postoperative 29.3% to 33.7%). Intervention failed preoperatively; ADL at discharge improved and unit stay fell by 2.5 days, with no change in complications.

PMID:35940697.setting: Changi General Hospital, 1000-bed hospital in eastern Singapore; anaesthesia department QI project
PMID:35940697.standard: Surgery within 48 hours of hip fracture; aims of a 10% increase in patients seen by anaesthesia within 24 hours and a 10% increase in surgery within 48 hours

cycle1.result: Median time to first anaesthesia consult 35.3 hours; consults <24 hours 39%; median time to surgery 61.5 hours; surgery within 48 hours 38%.

PMID:35940697.intervention: Consultant-led anaesthesia perioperative outreach service seeing patients within 24 hours of admission, with case manager notification, REDCap follow-up database, standardised workflow and guidelines, and 6-monthly PDSA audits.

cycle2.result: Median time to anaesthesia consult 21.5 hours (p = 0.029); consults <24 hours 67% (p < 0.003); median time to surgery 46 hours in results (50 hours in abstract) (p = 0.897); surgery within 48 hours 51.6% (p = 0.904).

PMID:35940697.other_findings: Median time to nerve block fell from 41 hours (2019) to 22 hours (2021); patients discharged within 10 days rose from 53.5% to 59.5%. Critical care reviews rose while ICU admissions fell.

PMID:40828478.setting: Sprint audit of 31 hospitals (24 Australia, 7 New Zealand) in the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry; patients on DOACs versus other or no antithrombotics
PMID:40828478.standard: ANZ hip fracture clinical care standard and international consensus: surgery within 36 hours (including for patients on DOACs)

cycle1.result: Median time to surgery 39 h (IQR 24–48) on DOACs, 25 h (IQR 20–39) on no antithrombotic and 27 h (IQR 20–44) on other antithrombotics; DOAC patients had higher odds of surgery >36 h (aOR 3.65, 95% CI 2.40–5.55); 43% of DOAC patients had surgery within 36 h versus 61% on other antithrombotics.

PMID:40828478.other_findings: 18% (192) were on DOACs; transfusion rates did not differ (23% vs 17% vs 22%). Only 5/24 Australian and all 7 New Zealand hospitals had a DOAC protocol, and 73% restarted DOACs >48 h after surgery.

PMID:42221965.topic: Secondary fracture prevention after hip fracture
PMID:42221965.setting: Orthogeriatric co-managed ward, Beijing Jishuitan Hospital, tertiary hospital
PMID:42221965.standard: UK Fracture Liaison Service Database (FFFAP) key performance indicators (7 of 11 KPIs assessed), benchmarked against UK FFFAP 2016–2018 figures

cycle1.result: BMD screening 97.1% (2,610/2,689); bone-protective medication before discharge 94.0% (2,454/2,610); follow-up 50.7% at 90 days, 17.7% at 12–16 weeks, 9.5% at 12 months. 2018 KPIs: FLS assessment within 90 days 57.1% (UK 67.0%), falls assessment 87.5%, bone therapy recommended 94.3%, adherence at 12 months 11.6% (UK 18.8%).

PMID:42221965.other_findings: Falls assessment rose from 11.4% (2016) to 87.5% (2018) and DXA-only scanning fell to 14.1% in 2018 as QCT replaced it. Secondary fracture rates stayed at 11.0–13.4% across follow-up points.

PMID:38609852.topic: Proximal humeral fracture admission and length of stay
PMID:38609852.setting: Western Health, single large tertiary health service (Footscray, Sunshine and Williamstown hospitals); retrospective audit of records

cycle1.result: 39.4% (276) admitted to hospital; median length of stay 23 days (IQR 7, 48.5); 15.5% (109) needed a new discharge destination. Higher Charlson Comorbidity Index was associated with admission, longer stay and new discharge destination.

PMID:38609852.other_findings: Living with family/friends or in a care facility before injury was associated with lower admission and shorter stay; surgical treatment was associated with shorter stay (IRR 0.56). Older age and dementia were associated with a new discharge destination.

PMID:35642472.setting: IMPACT international multicentre audit collaboration (Scottish Hip Fracture Audit and partners); commentary
PMID:35642472.other_findings: Commentary on lessons from the IMPACT hip fracture audits in 2020, recommending reporting standards and a strategy for rapid collaborative audits and data-sharing in future outbreaks.

PMID:407532.other_findings: Title only: describes the rationale for criteria for a medical audit of total knee replacement.
